exercises.name: Boxing Stance & Guard
instructions: Stand side-on at roughly 45 degrees with your feet about shoulder-width apart and your weaker-side foot in front.
Soften both knees, share your weight evenly across both feet, and lift the rear heel slightly off the floor.
Bring both fists up with the lead hand near eye level and the rear fist beside your chin, elbows tucked toward your ribs.
Tuck your chin behind the lead shoulder, keep the hands closed but loose, and hold the position while breathing steadily.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing tall and square with the chin lifted, or planting both heels flat so the feet cannot move quickly.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold for short blocks in front of a mirror and shake the arms out between holds.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Every punch, step, and defensive move starts from and returns to this position.

exercises.name: Jab
instructions: Set your boxing stance with both hands up and your chin tucked.
Shift a little weight toward the lead leg and turn the trunk slightly as the lead arm travels straight out from the guard.
Rotate the fist so the knuckles face up and the palm faces the floor as the arm reaches full length.
Pull the hand back along the same straight line to your guard while the rear hand stays beside your chin.
exercises.commonMistakes: Drawing the hand back before punching, or letting the rear hand drift away from the chin.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise slowly in front of a mirror from a still stance before adding a step.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The lead straight punch sets range and rhythm for everything else you throw.

exercises.name: Cross
exercises.musclesWorked: Shoulders, chest, triceps, obliques, glutes, calves
instructions: Start in your boxing stance with the lead hand high and the lead elbow covering your ribs.
Turn the rear foot about a quarter turn on the ball of the foot and rotate the hips and trunk toward the lead side.
Extend the rear arm straight to the target, turning the palm down just before full reach.
Bring the hand back along the same path and settle into your stance with the elbow tucked.
exercises.formCue: Turn the hip, then the hand.
exercises.commonMistakes: Throwing with the arm only while the rear heel stays planted, or over-rotating and falling across your front foot.
exercises.beginnerModification: Rehearse the hip and foot turn with hands on your cheeks before adding the arm.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The rear straight teaches you to move force from the floor through the hips into the hand.

exercises.name: Lead Hook
instructions: From your stance, keep the rear hand tight to your chin and load a little weight onto the lead leg.
Lift the lead elbow to about shoulder height with the arm bent close to 90 degrees.
Drive off the front foot, lift the lead heel, and rotate the hips and trunk so the bent arm is carried through in an arc.
Stop the fist at your centre line, then bring it back to the guard by the shortest route.
exercises.formCue: Turn the body, the arm just follows.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pulling the hand back to wind up, or straightening the arm so the punch turns into a wide swing.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the hip turn with the arm already raised and fixed at 90 degrees.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The hook trains fast trunk rotation around a stable base.

exercises.name: Rear Hook
instructions: From your stance, keep the lead hand up beside your chin.
Rotate the trunk toward the lead side and shift weight onto the lead leg as the rear heel lifts.
Swing the rear arm through with the elbow held near 90 degrees and the knuckles pointing at the target.
Keep your eyes over the top of the arm, then return the hand to the guard by the shortest path.
exercises.formCue: Elbow bent, eyes over the arm.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the arm straighten into a loop, or dropping the lead hand while the rear hand travels.
exercises.beginnerModification: Slow the punch down and stop at the centre line until you can finish balanced.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds rotation from the rear side and balances the lead hook.

exercises.name: Lead Uppercut
instructions: From your stance, bend the knees a little and turn the upper body slightly toward the lead side.
Shift weight onto the lead leg while the rear hand stays high and firm against your chin.
Turn the lead fist so the knuckles point forward and drive it upward with the elbow kept bent.
Finish around chin height, then retract along the same path into your guard.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dropping the hand low to wind up, or leaning back and lifting the chin as the punch rises.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the small knee dip and rise with both hands glued to your cheeks first.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The uppercut links leg drive to a short, compact arm path.

exercises.name: Rear Uppercut
instructions: From your guard, shift weight onto the rear foot and turn the rear palm to face you.
Bend the rear knee slightly and lift the rear heel.
Drive up through the legs and hips and throw a short punch upward with the forearm close to vertical.
Keep your chin behind the lead shoulder, then bring the hand straight back to the guard.
exercises.commonMistakes: Winding up before the punch, or driving the fist across the body instead of upward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Work it slowly on the spot and stop the fist at chin height.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches upward drive from the hips with the guard still intact.

exercises.name: Jab to the Body
instructions: From your stance, bend the knees until your lead shoulder is level with a target at stomach height.
Keep the back straight, eyes forward, and the rear hand high.
Extend the lead arm straight out with a small hip turn, palm turning down at full reach.
Retract the hand and stand back up into your guard in one motion.
exercises.formCue: Bend the knees, not the waist.
exercises.commonMistakes: Folding at the waist and punching downward, which leaves the head forward and the chin open.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the level change alone as a small squat in stance before adding the punch.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Changing level with the legs adds real leg work to every round.

exercises.name: Lead Hook to the Body
instructions: From your stance, bend the knees until your lead shoulder lines up with a target at rib height.
Keep the rear hand firm against your chin and rotate the trunk slightly toward the lead side.
Shift weight to the lead leg and swing the lead arm through with the elbow bent near 90 degrees.
Return the hand by the shortest path and rise back into your stance.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dropping the hand instead of bending the knees, or letting the rear hand fall away from the chin.
exercises.beginnerModification: Throw it slowly in the air and pause in the lowered position to check your guard.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It combines a level change with rotation, which makes rounds more demanding on legs and trunk.

exercises.name: Jab-Cross-Hook Combo
instructions: Start in your stance and throw a straight jab that snaps back to the guard.
Follow with the cross, turning the rear foot and hip so weight moves toward the front leg.
Let that loaded position feed the lead hook, rotating back the other way with the elbow bent.
Finish balanced in your stance with both hands at your chin before repeating.
exercises.commonMistakes: Throwing three separate punches with pauses, or over-committing to the cross and stumbling into the hook.
exercises.beginnerModification: Drill jab-cross until it is smooth, then add the hook at half speed.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Short combinations teach each punch to set up the body position for the next.

exercises.name: Double Jab-Cross
instructions: From your stance, throw a jab and bring it only part of the way back.
Throw a second jab straight away, with a small forward step if you have room.
Follow with the cross, rotating the rear hip and foot.
Recover both hands to the guard and reset your feet to shoulder width.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the feet come together on the step, or dropping the jab hand between the two jabs.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise on the spot without the step until the rhythm is steady.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Repeating the lead hand builds shoulder endurance and timing for the rear hand.

exercises.name: Boxing Pivot
exercises.musclesWorked: Calves, quads, glutes, hip rotators, core
instructions: Set your stance with your weight centred and both hands up.
Push off the rear foot and spin on the ball of the lead foot.
Swing the rear foot around behind you so your stance turns about 45 degrees.
Land in the same stance width and repeat, then practise turning the other way.
exercises.formCue: Front foot spins, back foot swings.
exercises.commonMistakes: Crossing the legs or tipping weight forward over the lead knee during the turn.
exercises.beginnerModification: Make smaller turns and pause after each one to check your stance width.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Pivoting changes your angle without giving up balance.

exercises.name: Step-Drag Footwork
instructions: Stand in your boxing stance on the balls of your feet.
To go forward, lift the lead foot slightly, push off the rear foot, and slide the rear foot up once the lead foot lands.
To go back, lift the rear foot slightly, push off the lead foot, and slide the lead foot back to stance width.
Keep the feet shoulder-width apart and your weight shared across both legs throughout.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bringing the feet together, crossing them, or moving flat-footed on the heels.
exercises.beginnerModification: Take small steps along a line on the floor and reset your stance after each one.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Keeping your base while moving is what lets you punch from balance.

exercises.name: Boxing Side Step
instructions: Start in your boxing stance with the knees soft.
To move left in an orthodox stance, lift the lead foot slightly and push off the rear foot, then let the rear foot follow.
To move right, lift the rear foot slightly and push off the lead foot, then let the lead foot follow.
Finish every step at shoulder width with the guard up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Taking one oversized step that stretches the stance, or letting the feet click together.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use short steps and pause in stance between each one.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Lateral steps take you off a straight line while keeping you ready to work.

exercises.name: Pull Counter
exercises.musclesWorked: Obliques, spinal erectors, glutes, shoulders, calves
instructions: From your guard, shift weight onto the rear leg and lean the upper body back a few centimetres.
Keep both hands up and your chin down as you lean.
Push off the rear foot to bring your weight forward again.
Throw a straight rear hand as you return, then recover to your balanced stance.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning so far that the head lifts and the base is lost, or dropping the lead hand on the way back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the weight shift back and forward without the punch.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains quick weight transfer between the back and front leg.

exercises.name: Shadow Parry Drill
instructions: Stand in your guard and picture a straight punch coming toward your face.
Turn the body slightly toward the lead side and make a short inward tap with the rear hand, as if deflecting it at the wrist.
Keep the elbow in and stop the hand before it crosses your face.
Return the hand to your chin at once, then answer with a jab.
exercises.commonMistakes: Reaching out to meet the imaginary punch, or sweeping the hand wide across the face.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the parry alone in a mirror before adding the jab.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Small, economical hand defence keeps the guard in place and frees the other hand.

exercises.name: Duck Under
instructions: Stand in your guard with your eyes forward.
Bend both knees down and slightly inward so your head drops straight below its starting height.
Keep the forearms and elbows covering the body and keep looking ahead.
Drive back up into your stance with the hands still in place.
exercises.commonMistakes: Folding at the waist and looking at the floor, or tipping the weight onto the front leg.
exercises.beginnerModification: Reduce the depth and move slowly until you can stay upright through the trunk.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Ducking with the legs turns defence practice into steady lower-body work.

exercises.name: Speed Bag Rhythm
instructions: Stand square to the bag at about arm's length with the bottom of the bag near eye level.
Hold both hands up close to the bag and strike with small circles instead of back-and-forth swings.
Let the bag rebound three times after each strike before you hit it again.
Work a steady pattern of two strikes with one hand and then two with the other.
exercises.commonMistakes: Holding the hands too far from the bag, or swinging hard and losing the rhythm.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with open hands and one strike at a time until the three-rebound count feels natural.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds shoulder endurance and hand-eye timing.

exercises.name: Double-End Bag Rounds
instructions: Set the bag so the ball sits around head height and take your stance at jab range.
Start with single jabs and time each one as the ball returns to centre.
Add the cross, then simple two and three punch combinations at a steady rhythm.
Keep your feet moving and your guard up between combinations for the whole round.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing flat-footed, or hitting hard so the ball swings out of control.
exercises.beginnerModification: Work only the jab for the first rounds and shorten the round length.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A moving target trains accuracy and timing more than power.

exercises.name: Teep (Push Kick)
exercises.musclesWorked: Hip flexors, quads, glutes, core, calves
instructions: Stand in your stance with hands up and shift your weight onto the back leg.
Lift the lead knee toward your chest.
Push the foot straight forward, driving the hips toward the target and leaning back only slightly.
Pull the knee back in and set the foot down in your stance.
exercises.commonMistakes: Flicking the lower leg without the hip drive, or dropping the hands as the leg lifts.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the knee lift and balance hold, and kick at knee to waist height only.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The push kick builds single-leg balance and hip drive.

exercises.name: Roundhouse Kick
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hip rotators, obliques, quads, calves
instructions: From your stance with fists by your chin, step the base foot slightly out and rise onto the ball of that foot.
Turn the base foot away from the kick as you lift the kicking knee to point at the target.
Rotate the hips over and swing the leg through horizontally, meeting a bag with the shin.
Bring the leg back and return to your stance with the guard up.
exercises.formCue: Pivot the base foot, turn the hip over.
exercises.commonMistakes: Kicking with a flat, unturned base foot, or kicking higher than you can control so the trunk folds.
exercises.beginnerModification: Kick slowly in the air at knee to hip height while holding a wall or chair for balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The roundhouse trains hip rotation and balance on one leg.

exercises.name: Low Kick
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hip rotators, obliques, quads, calves
instructions: Stand in your stance at a range where your shin can reach the lower part of a heavy bag.
Step out slightly and pivot on the ball of the base foot.
Turn the hip and swing the leg through to meet the bag at thigh height with the shin.
Recover the leg to your stance and reset your guard.
exercises.commonMistakes: Reaching with the foot instead of the shin, or leaving the base foot planted flat.
exercises.beginnerModification: Rehearse in the air at slow speed before working lightly on a bag.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The low line lets you practise full hip rotation without needing much flexibility.

exercises.name: Switch Kick
exercises.musclesWorked: Calves, glutes, hip rotators, obliques, quads
instructions: Stand in your stance with the guard up.
Step the lead foot back and the rear foot forward in one quick switch, staying close to the floor.
As the new rear foot lands, pivot on the base foot and throw a roundhouse with the leg that started in front.
Bring the leg back and return to your original stance.
exercises.commonMistakes: Jumping both feet high in the air at once, which wastes time and upsets balance.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the stance switch alone, then add a slow knee lift before kicking.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The switch adds quick footwork and coordination to the basic kick.

exercises.name: Straight Knee Strike
instructions: Stand in your stance with hands high, or reach both hands forward as if holding a bag.
Push off the floor with the rear foot and drive that knee forward and up.
Push the hips forward and rise onto the ball of the standing foot as the knee reaches its peak.
Set the foot back down in your stance and reset before the next rep.
exercises.commonMistakes: Lifting the knee without pushing the hips through, or rounding forward over the knee.
exercises.beginnerModification: Slow it down and hold a wall for balance while you learn the hip drive.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Knee strikes work the hip flexors and trunk while challenging single-leg balance.

exercises.name: Shadow Elbow Strike
instructions: Stand in your stance with a high guard and no target in front of you.
Fold one arm so the hand stays near your chest and lift the elbow to shoulder height.
Rotate from the trunk and hips to carry the elbow across in a short horizontal arc.
Keep the other hand against your face, return to the guard, and alternate sides and angles.
exercises.formCue: Turn from the middle, other hand stays home.
exercises.commonMistakes: Over-rotating and losing balance, or dropping the guard hand during the turn.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise slowly facing a mirror, one angle at a time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Elbow shadow work is compact rotation practice for the trunk and shoulders.

exercises.name: Kick Check
instructions: Stand in your stance with hands up.
Shift your weight onto the back leg.
Lift the lead knee up and turn it slightly outward so the shin faces to the side, with the same-side elbow close above the knee.
Hold for a moment in balance, then set the foot down in your stance.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning forward as the leg lifts, or letting the hands drop for balance.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lift the knee lower and hold a wall lightly with one hand.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The check is a balance drill that strengthens the standing leg and hip.

exercises.name: Technical Stand-Up
instructions: Sit on the floor with one hand posted behind you and the opposite foot flat on the floor.
Hold the free hand up in front of your face.
Press through the posted hand and foot to lift your hips, then swing the free leg back underneath you.
Plant that foot behind you and stand up into a staggered stance, then sit back down and switch sides.
exercises.formCue: Hand and opposite foot, hips up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Trying to stand without lifting the hips first, or placing the back foot too close to the posted hand.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise only the hip lift and leg swing before standing all the way up.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is a controlled way to get from the floor to your feet with a stable base.

exercises.name: Bridge and Roll
instructions: Lie on your back with your feet flat and your heels close to your hips.
Drive through your feet to lift your hips high.
Turn to look over one shoulder and reach the opposite arm across your body as you bridge onto that shoulder.
Lower back to the start, or roll through to your knees, and repeat on the other side.
exercises.commonMistakes: Turning before the hips are lifted, or pushing through the neck instead of the shoulder.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do straight glute bridges first, then add a small turn onto the shoulder.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds explosive hip extension with rotation.

exercises.name: Penetration Step
instructions: Start in a low athletic stance with knees bent and back flat.
Lower your hips to change level while keeping your chest and head up.
Step forward with the lead leg and let the lead knee glide toward the mat as the hips drive forward.
Bring the trail leg up and through to return to your stance, then repeat down the mat.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending at the waist with the head down, or stepping so far that the trail leg cannot follow.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a shorter step and keep the knee off the mat until the level change feels smooth.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains a fast level change and forward drive from the legs.

exercises.name: Sit-Through
instructions: Start on your hands and feet with knees bent and hovering just off the floor.
Lift one hand and the opposite foot.
Thread the lifted leg underneath your body and rotate your hips until that hip faces the floor beside you.
Bring the leg back to the start and repeat to the other side.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the hips drop to the floor and rest, or rushing so the supporting shoulder collapses.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start from hands and knees and move slowly through a smaller range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds shoulder stability and rotational hip mobility under bodyweight.

exercises.name: Wrestling Stance and Motion
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, calves, core, upper back
instructions: Take a staggered or square stance with knees bent, hips low, back flat, and hands in front of you.
Move in short steps forward, back, and in a circle without crossing your feet.
Move your feet whenever your hands move so you never reach from a still base.
Every few steps, drop your hips to change level and rise back to your stance.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing up between steps, or crossing the feet while circling.
exercises.beginnerModification: Work in shorter bursts and hold a higher stance until the legs adapt.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Holding a low stance while moving builds leg endurance fast.
